elements.text: Cessna 441 pilot's mistaken belief that his assigned departure runway was runway 30R
Cessna 441 pilot's undetected entrance onto runway 30R
Lack of ATIS and other ATC information regarding the occasional use of runway 31 for departure
Cessna 441 pilot acted on preconceived idea to use arrival runway 30R for departure
Cessna 441 pilot taxied into position at an intersection on runway 30R instead of assigned runway 31
Pilot's desire to return home before weather deteriorated contributed to mistaken actions
Pilot did not read back the runway assignment in ATC clearance
Controller did not use more precise phraseology in initial taxi clearance
Lack of runway assignment confirmation by pilot or controller
ATC personnel unable to maintain visual contact with Cessna 441 after leaving ramp area
Absence of operational ASDE-3 (especially with AMASS) to supplement visual scan
Cessna 441 exterior lighting directed forward, limiting visibility to MD-82
Likely non-operational wing anticollision/strobe lights on Cessna 441
MD-82 flightcrew did not observe external lights on Cessna 441 before impact
MD-82 flightcrew and Cessna 441 pilot were properly certificated and qualified
Air traffic control personnel were properly certificated and qualified
Both airplanes were properly certificated and maintained
Cessna 441 pilot had communication radio difficulties that did not contribute to the accident
Airfield markings, signs, and lighting conformed to FAA standards
Inoperative light bulbs on position signs were clearly visible and not a factor
Runway 31 displaced threshold was properly marked and lighted
ARFF emergency response was timely and effective, preventing further serious injuries
MD-82 evacuation was orderly and organized
Ground controller workload was moderate but involved working seven frequencies
ATIS listed runways 30R and 30L as active, with no mention of occasional use of runway 31
Pilot training for surface movement can be improved
Investigation notification and team dispatch details
List of parties to the investigation
